info.bio:
Timothy Charles Buckley III (14 de febrero de 1947 – 29 de junio de 1975) fue un músico estadounidense de rock de vanguardia, con influencias de jazz, psicodelia, funk y soul. Su carrera fue corta, entre finales de los 60 y los primeros 70.

La voz de Buckley llegaba a abarcar tres octavas y media. Su talento con la voz está patente en álbumes como Goodbye and Hello (1967), Lorca (1970) y Starsailor (1970). Se casó con Mari Guibert, con la que tuvo un hijo, Jeff Buckley, conocido por su voz de cuatro octavas y media, que murió en 1997.

scenes.name: Excéntricos y art rock de los setenta
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: El mito punk del «páramo» prepunk escondía uno de los periodos más ricos del rock. Con cautela, para no parecer hippies encubiertos, los grupos postpunk recuperan a excéntricos como Captain Beefheart y las aristas más agudas del progresivo: Soft Machine, King Crimson, incluso Frank Zappa. «En cierto sentido, el postpunk era rock progresivo» racionalizado, sin virtuosismo.
scenes.family: Antecedentes: punk, art rock, kraut y glam

scenes.name: Folk-rock
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Más invento de productores (Tom Wilson, Terry Melcher) que movimiento artístico: el espíritu del Mersey-beat en clave americana. Byrds y Beau Brummels crean el «jingle-jangle»; los Byrds encadenan folk-rock, acid-rock, raga-rock («Eight Miles High») y country-rock (Sweetheart Of The Rodeo). Mamas & Papas, Turtles, Lovin' Spoonful, Buffalo Springfield y, sobre todo, Tim Buckley, que funde folk, blues, jazz, psicodelia y música de cámara y convierte la voz en un instrumento (Happy Sad, Lorca, Starsailor).

Tim Buckley (122) synthesized a new genre of music by fusing folk, blues, jazz, psychedelic rock and chamber music. Very few rock musicians ever achieved the monstrous intensity and lyrical tenderness of his work. Buckley's songs were journeys through the psyche of the singer. Buckley was therefore more interested in mirroring the emotions of the soul than in emphasizing a melody. A Buckley song is a stream of consciousness. Buckley changed the very idea of what a folk or rock song is supposed to be. podcast.title: Classic American Singer-Songwriter
podcast.body: Tim Buckley is described as one of the "grandes nombres clásicos americanos" (great classic American names). Despite his talent, he did not achieve widespread success during his relatively short career. A memorial concert was held in his honor, at which his son, Jeff Buckley, performed his songs, marking a pivotal moment in Jeff's own emerging career. "hijo de Tim Buckley uno de esos agrandomores clásicos americanos no tenía mucho éxito en su corta carrera."

podcast.title: Critical Acclaim vs. Commercial Recognition
podcast.body: Although critics highly praised his albums, Tim Buckley's talent was not widely recognized until after his death in 1975. At the time of his passing, he was deeply in debt, owning only the clothes he wore, a guitar, and an amplifier. "Critics loved his albums, but he wasn't recognized for the talent that he was until well after he died in 1975 of what appears to be a heroine overdose at age 28. He was very deep in debt, and at the time of his death, owned nothing more than the clothes on his back, a guitar, and an amplifier."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Life and Marriage
podcast.body: Tim Buckley began his career as a folk singer in the 1960s. He met Mary Guibert in French class in high school in 1964 and married her in 1965. However, their marriage ended in divorce about a month before their son, Jeff, was born. "He began as a folk singer back in the 1960s. In 1964, he met Mary Gebert in French class in high school and eventually married her in 1965. However, that didn't work out. And about a month before their son was born, Tim and Mary divorced."

podcast.title: Musical Evolution and Self-Destructive Behavior
podcast.body: After his divorce, Tim Buckley dedicated himself full-time to music, exploring a wide range of genres including folk, psych, jazz, funk, and soul. Simultaneously, he engaged in self-destructive behaviors. "Tim went into music full-time, cycling through folk, psych, bits of jazz, fun, and soul, while also pursuing some pretty self-destructive behavior."

xref.title: Early Influences and Musical Development
xref.body: Jeff Buckley, born to Tim Buckley and Mary Guibert, met his father only once. His mother was a classically trained musician, while his stepfather introduced him to bands like Pink Floyd, Jimi Hendrix, The Who, Led Zeppelin, and Queen. Jeff picked up the guitar at age 5, discovered Rush, Kiss, and various prog rock bands, and received his first electric guitar at age 12. "One of the people Tim left behind was his eight-year-old son, Jeff, who admitted his father only once. Mom was a classically trained musician playing piano and cello. Meanwhile, Jeff's death father was into Pink Floyd, Jimmy Hendrix, the who led Zeppelin and Queen. He picked up a guitar at age 5, discovered rush and kiss and various prog rock bands, which led to his first electric guitar at age 12."
